build: PAL two-sided G64 supplied by the contributor; EA loader, no trainer observed

exclude: High Jump zero page holds mutable input, movement, sound and graphics state, not authored image bytes

comments.text: Inline NUL-terminated header text printed by the call at $099E through $1242: spaces, PASS:, spaces, HEIGHT:, spaces. These are text bytes, not calls to $2020 or $4150.

High Jump raster-band update: wait for line $3A, set VIC display controls, read joystick/keyboard ports, run event update and drawing calls, then repeat late-frame work until raster $DC or ten iterations.
Read and combine active-low CIA1 ports into $2F/$30, then dispatch through the event input table at $2AB9. The following loop advances counters and calls event state/drawing routines.
State $00 handler: reset temporary movement fields, sample position and fire-related input, advance $31/$32 timing counters, update the skater display pose, and possibly switch to state $0C.
State $0C handler: update skater position, sample fire, advance $31/$32 through a pose table selected by $33, and return to state $00 when input or the table limit says so.
State $02 handler: update movement and position, select a pose from the $2A17 group by coordinate $23 and facing, then choose the next state through $2A11 when $23 crosses $96.
State $06 handler: update moving position, choose pose from indexed tables, increment $31/$32 timing counters, adjust the skater coordinate and transition to state $00 or $10 at its bounds.
State $04 handler: update movement, process directional control bits and pose flags, and choose state $02, $06 or $08 according to position and pose tests.
State $08 handler: advance an animation through seven entries at the pointer $1C, updating pose $4F every second tick, then enter state $0A.
State $0A handler: advance the same animation in reverse, sample fire at its start, update pose and return to state $04 after seven entries.
State $0E handler: advance a seven-entry pose sequence every sixth tick, choose its facing table by $24 and then enter state $10.
State $10 handler: reset temporary fields, advance a ten-tick pose sequence, choose a sprite table by stored height $2B, and on completion with fire released jump to $1A49.
Compute skater display coordinates in $49/$4A and $4B from motion indices $51/$52 and position fields $46/$47, using paired lookup differences; the sign of $48 selects the horizontal reflection path.
Pull the caller return address, read following NUL-terminated inline bytes, mask each with $3F and render its inverted glyph, then return after the terminator.
Treat A as an eight-byte index into $6800, invert each source byte, copy eight bytes to the destination pointer $14/$15, then advance that pointer by eight.
Use signed position $54/$55 and facing bit in $48 to select a two-byte position from the table at $2ACB, or clamp to an endpoint; write the result to $46/$47 and report clamping in carry.
Given indices A and Y, form the absolute index difference, use it to subtract paired lookup values at $0400/$0600 from values at $048F/$068F, and return the two resulting bytes in A and Y.
Build a 64-byte output block through the $2E7B byte lookup table: zero the unused tail, transform source bytes into destination bytes, then advance the six-byte descriptor and output pointer.
Like expand_graphics_with_table_a but map each source byte through the lookup table at $2F7B.
Build a 64-byte output block by zeroing its unused tail and copying the remaining source bytes directly, then advance descriptor and output pointers.

Toggle the output graphics buffer via $22, find a descriptor in the $7000 region from the pose index, then build four or five 64-byte graphics blocks using direct copy or lookup-table transforms according to the state sign bits.

Set High Jump phase from A (observed cases $00,$02,$06,$08,$10), reset phase counters $31/$32, and initialize distinct movement, position and sound fields for each case. The game meaning of each phase still needs a live trace.
Render the High Jump HEIGHT number from $2B: upper five bits index a two-glyph feet table at $2DC7, low three bits index rounded-inch glyphs at $2DF1, with punctuation glyphs inserted between them.
Sound scheduler header: pending-event count, current priority and selected slot, followed by mutable script pointers and per-voice timers; initialized by $22B7 and serviced at $232C.
Per-slot SID script timers, sound IDs, gate/control bytes and priorities, indexed by slot offsets 0, 2 and 4 in the updater at $232C.
Sixteen-byte pending sound ID queue; $22F5 appends an ID while count at $221B is below $10, and $232C drains it into queue_sid_sound.
First resident sound-script bytes. Sound init at $22B7 installs pointers to $2287, $2297 and $22A7; the bytecode format is not yet decoded.
Drain pending sound IDs through queue_sid_sound, then iterate three SID voice slots (offsets 4,2,0): count down gate and script timers, fetch script commands and update voice control.
Fetch the next byte through the current voice script pointer at $02/$03 indexed by X, then increment that pointer with carry.
Use the low nibble of the command byte to select one of 16 split high/low handler addresses at $23AE/$23BE; push the address as an RTS target and pass the high nibble in A.
High bytes of 16 primary SID bytecode handler addresses, paired with low bytes at $23BE; $2394 dispatches by low command nibble.
Low bytes of 16 primary SID bytecode handler addresses, paired with high bytes at $23AE; handlers run at stored address plus one after RTS.
Primary SID bytecode handler: use command argument to set frequency, pulse width, attack/decay, sustain/release, control or a voice timer, reading immediate script bytes or a referenced value.
Fetch a sound ID from the active script and append it through $22F5, preserving the current voice-slot registers.

Sound bytecode handler that reads a two-byte address from the script, then writes a value there or compares against a value; a failed comparison rewinds the script pointer and leaves the current interpreter dispatch.
Sound bytecode handler that adds script-provided deltas to voice frequency, pulse width, sustain or timer fields and writes resulting SID registers when applicable.
Sound bytecode control-flow handler: conditional script branches, loop counters, queued sound IDs and saved return pointers. Some cases read direct bytes and others use address-based operands.
Compare current voice frequency, pulse width, envelope or timer against script operands, and store the resulting comparison class in the voice state at $226C.

Interpret a secondary sound stream through $08/$09: compute frequency and envelope changes, update SID registers, load per-voice modulation data or dispatch through the secondary handler table at $27ED/$27F8.
Eleven split low/high addresses selected by the secondary sound command at $2752; each pair points to a routine in $2803-$28BD.
Secondary sound command: scale a two-byte delta, fetch a gate timer, then write the resulting two-byte frequency to the selected SID voice.
Secondary sound command: take a literal low and next high frequency byte, fetch gate timer, then write frequency to the selected SID voice.
Secondary sound command: scale a frequency delta, fetch gate and envelope timers, set the gate-timing flag, then write SID frequency.
Secondary sound command: use two literal frequency bytes, fetch gate and envelope timers, set gate-timing flag, then write SID frequency.
Store the per-voice shift amount for later scaled sound deltas, then continue interpreting the secondary stream.
Read four secondary-stream bytes into the selected voice table at $2235, then continue the stream.
Read four secondary-stream bytes into the selected voice table at $2241, then continue the stream.
Write the command byte to the selected SID control register and mirror it in voice state.
Write the command byte to the selected SID attack/decay register and mirror it in voice state.
Write the command byte to the selected SID sustain/release register and mirror it in voice state.
Write two secondary-stream bytes to the selected SID pulse-width registers and mirror them in voice state.
Select a two-byte sound delta from tables $29E1/$29F1 and shift it right by the command high-nibble amount plus the per-voice offset at $2271.
Fetch the next script byte as a voice timer; depending on the command sign bit, store it in the primary timer or the gate timer and mark gate timing active.
If no nested script is active, clear SID gate, voice state and current priority; otherwise pop the saved script pointer and resume the caller.
Fetch a two-byte address from the sound script and call it indirectly while preserving voice and SID register indices.
Fetch a two-byte address from the sound script and return the value at that address, with the following byte in $11; restore the SID register offset in Y.

Accept queued sound ID in A if its priority table entry meets the current threshold; choose one of three SID voice slots, load its script pointer from $307B/$3095, clear slot counters and seven registers of that SID voice.
Six slot offsets ($0E,$0E,$07,$07,$00,$00) select the base of a SID voice register group in queue_sid_sound and the per-frame sound updater at $2345.
Two little-endian interrupt callback addresses, $0B21 and $0CA3; the IRQ dispatcher at $0AF0 selects one through $1E and patches its call operand.
Nine little-endian code pointers, selected by even state value $2E at $0D3F and patched into the call at $0D4E. Entries cover states $00,$02,$04,$06,$08,$0A,$0C,$0E,$10.
First two entries are sound IDs chosen by the High Jump phase-$06 path at $16A2, using the in-range flag as index; the other entries in this run are not yet attributed.
Twenty-one two-glyph entries for feet 0 through 20, rendered by draw_height_digits from height byte $2B divided by eight.
Eight two-glyph rounded-inch entries for remainders 0 through 7: 00,02,03,05,06,08,09,11. Live tests gave $2B=$04 -> 0 feet 6 inches and $2B=$08 -> 1 foot 0 inches.
All 256 entries equal the input byte with its eight individual bits reversed; the graphics builder at $138D applies it while forming a 64-byte block.
All 256 entries equal the input byte with its four two-bit pixel pairs reversed; the graphics builder at $13C5 applies it while forming a 64-byte block.
Twenty-six sound-script addresses in split low/high arrays, indexed by the sound ID at $2994/$2999; the first points to $30CC.
Twenty-six one-byte priorities indexed by sound ID; $2982 compares the incoming value against the current voice threshold before allocation.
Compact event labels: $01-$1A are A-Z, $20 is space; this block reads RAMP HIGHJUMP and DOWNHILL JAM, with $FE/$FF framing bytes.
